question: Úplne prvý tovar na svete, ktorý pri pokladni načítali čiarovým kódom, bola drobnosť, akú dodnes nájdete hneď vedľa pokladničného pásu. Čo to bolo?
source_excerpt: first UPC-marked item scanned at a retail checkout was a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum, at Marsh supermarket in Troy, Ohio, on June 26, 1974

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a big symbolic first product, such as milk, bread or a famous brand. The answer is the small item still sitting at every checkout, and the stem's hint lets them reason their way to it.
extra.verification_notes: The first scanned retail item was a 10-pack of Wrigley's Juicy Fruit gum on 26 June 1974 in Troy, Ohio (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Universal_Product_Code).

explanation: Bol to balíček žuvačiek Wrigley's Juicy Fruit v supermarkete v americkom Ohiu a dnes je vystavený v múzeu Smithsonian.

question: Keď sa v Amerike objavili prvé nákupné vozíky, nikto ich nechcel tlačiť. Mužom pripadali nemužné a ženám pripomínali detský kočík. Ako ich majiteľ obchodu napokon dostal medzi ľudí?
alternative_answers: zaplatil ľuďom, aby s nimi nakupovali
source_excerpt: Sylvan Goldman hired several male and female models to push the carts around his store and show how useful they were.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the shopping cart caught on instantly because it is so obviously useful. In fact people refused to touch it, and the fix was a piece of social-proof theatre that players can work out themselves.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Goldman hired models to push carts in his store to demonstrate them, after men found them unmanly and women found them like baby carriages.

explanation: Sylvan Goldman z Oklahomy zaplatil modelom, aby s vozíkmi chodili po obchode. Keď ľudia videli, že ich používajú iní, rýchlo sa pridali.
